conviction_note: The H1 print for this pre-revenue biotech is really a cash-and-runway statement. The documents show the funding gap is wider than the last guided runway (end-December 2026) assumed: IRIS proceeds are tracking at roughly half the price that runway was built on, and a EUR 7m EIB tranche fell due in July 2026. But the refinancing need is the most-discussed fact on the name, and the stock is down 50% since the IRIS deal, 28% in 20 days and 12% in 5, which cuts against the +1.38 bounce lean. So a finding sum of -1.3 is shaded to -0.8, and cut further for a real chance (about 20-25%) that the release slips past the 29 Sep close, as the 2025 H1 did.
bar: Unsourced as a consensus: no EPS or cash consensus exists for this name (Yahoo consensus quarters are empty). The operative bar is the company's own runway guidance, 'Confirmed cash runway until the end of December 2026 after the IRIS Financing' (2026-06-03, https://fr.ftp.opendatasoft.com/datadila/INFOFI/MKW/2026/06/FCMKW115759_20260603.pdf). That guidance rests on IRIS gross proceeds of 'approximately EUR 19.3 million' priced at the 27 May VWAP of EUR 4.8297 (https://fr.ftp.opendatasoft.com/datadila/INFOFI/MKW/2026/05/FCMKW114627_20260528.pdf). Because it is not a two-source consensus, every size is capped small.
session_check: amc. The company's own investor page says 'Financial results are published after market close' and lists 'September 28, 2026 2026 First-Half Financial Update and Statements' (https://www.ose-immuno.com/en/investors-2/). The French page carries '28 septembre 2026 Résultats financiers du 1er semestre 2026' (https://www.ose-immuno.com/fr/investisseurs/), and so does the AMF-filed 2026 calendar of 2026-03-16 (https://fr.ftp.opendatasoft.com/datadila/INFOFI/MKW/2026/03/FCMKW130028_20260316.pdf). Past practice is mixed, which is why the date carries risk: FY2025 was calendared for 29 April and came out 30 April at 07:30 CEST (bmo, still inside an amc-28 window if the same thing happens), the audited FY followed on 3 June at 20:00 CET, and the H1 2025 results slipped to 15 Oct 2025 at 19:00 CEST. The calendar is 'donné à titre indicatif, sous réserve de modifications', so there is a slip risk I put at about 20-25%.
positioning_check: The AMF positions courtes nettes register was read (covered: true, as of 2026-09-21, https://www.data.gouv.fr/api/1/datasets/r/c2539d1c-8531-4937-9cba-3bd8e9786cc5) and does not name OSE: 0.0%, change 0.0 pts, anchor_covered false. That is the 0.5% truncation floor, not evidence that nobody is short, so this name has no positioning anchor and priced_lean_pct (+1.38) is purely the run-up term. The visible supply is the IRIS equity line instead: 200,000 / 466,000 / 599,000 new shares issued in June / July / August 2026 per the AMF voting-rights filings.

findings.finding: The runway the market was last given (end-December 2026, 3 June) assumed about EUR 19.3m of IRIS proceeds priced at the EUR 4.83 VWAP. With spot at EUR 2.31, the 2,735,000 warrants left after 1,265,000 shares were issued in June-August are worth only about EUR 6m at the 5% discount. The URD also schedules a EUR 7m EIB repayment for July 2026 and says about EUR 15m more is needed for a 12-month runway. So the H1 release's cash-at-30-June and runway/going-concern language is more likely to shorten, or to be made conditional on a new financing, than to reaffirm.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Price moves after this name's financial and funding releases (Yahoo OSE.PA daily closes): H1 2025 results (15 Oct 2025, amc) -7.5% the next day; H1 2025 cash position (25 Sep 2025, amc) -1.8%; FY2025 unaudited plus Q1 cash and 'runway until early Q4 2026' (30 Apr 2026, bmo) -3.3%; IRIS bridge (28 May 2026, amc) -7.9% the next day, then -4.6% and -8.5%; audited FY with 'runway end-December 2026' (3 Jun 2026, amc) +0.1%. Funding news has been sold every time but once.
findings.original_quote: URD 2025 (English): 'based on current assumptions (including the IRIS financing and the repayment of the €7 million tranche due to the EIB in July 2026) ... its activities are financed until end of December 2026 ... In order to secure a cash runway of at least twelve months from the date of this Universal Registration Document, the Company estimates that additional funding of approximately €15 million would be required.' AMF filing of 7 Sep 2026 (French): 'Incluant 599.000 actions nouvelles émises au cours du mois d'août 2026 dans le cadre du financement relais flexible en fonds propres avec IRIS Capital Investment' (Including 599,000 new shares issued during August 2026 under the flexible bridge equity financing with IRIS Capital Investment); July: 466.000; June: 200.000 (https://fr.ftp.opendatasoft.com/datadila/INFOFI/MKW/2026/09/FCMKW131349_20260907.pdf, .../2026/08/FCMKW139461_20260826.pdf, .../2026/07/FCMKW131885_20260708.pdf).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced, and that is why it is small. If the market had fully priced a going-concern cliff, the IRIS shares would not still be absorbing near 5% discounts and the stock would trade nearer cash; it is on an all-time low but still well above that. What has NOT been published is the 30 June cash figure. The company has put out no Q2 cash position, and its calendar has no such date. Nor has it said whether the July EIB tranche was repaid or rescheduled: the AMF flux shows no EIB filing since June. The runway re-statement that follows from those numbers is also unpublished. The sign is genuinely open, because a larger raise with specialist funds that ends the IRIS overhang could be taken as relief (Biomed Impact, 29 May: 'une levée de fonds significative avec des fonds de qualité peut induire un regain de confiance'). Hence the wide band on both sides.
findings.independence: Same document family as the company releases (URD, AMF filings, IRIS release), so no independent confirmation of the numbers. A different source agrees that refinancing is the central open question: Biomed Impact, 3 Sep 2026, 'Le titre devrait réagir positivement mais de façon modérée en raison du sujet de refinancement qui reste central sur le dossier' (The stock should react positively but moderately, because refinancing remains the central issue) — https://www.biomed-impact.com/post/commentaire-ose-immuno-03-09-2026 — and on 29 May it expected 'un montage plus conséquent d'ici 3-6 mois' (a larger financing within 3-6 months) — https://www.biomed-impact.com/post/commentaire-ose-immuno-29-05-2026.

findings.finding: The ARTEMIA Phase 3 interim futility analysis was guided to Q3 2026, but the same release put the next IDMC review in October 2026. Nothing has been filed by 25 Sep, so the H1 release's milestone section will most likely move this key catalyst into Q4. That makes it a small guidance-timing negative inside the window; the binary outcome itself sits outside it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean prior re-dating of an ARTEMIA milestone to measure. The nearest pipeline-reset release, the 2 Mar 2026 refocusing/pause of OSE-230 and CLEC-1, was followed by weakness that Biomed Impact had predicted ('Le titre devrait réagir plutôt négativement'). IDMC 'continue' recommendations have not produced large moves.
findings.original_quote: English release: 'The next IDMC review is scheduled for October 2026.' / 'Tedopi® NSCLC Pivotal Phase 3 interim futility analysis is expected in Q3 2026.' French corroboration, Biomed Impact 3 Mar 2026: 'l'analyse intermédiaire de futilité au T3 de l'étude de Phase III ARTEMIA' (the interim futility analysis in Q3 of the Phase III ARTEMIA study).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely telegraphed: the February release already carried the October IDMC date, and French retail forums were counting down the days ('Toujours pas de futilité à 10 jours de la fin du T3', Boursorama forum, 21 Sep — opinion, not evidence). What the market does not yet have is a formal re-dating. Only that residual is sized.
findings.independence: Biomed Impact 3 Mar 2026 independently records the Q3 futility timing: https://www.biomed-impact.com/post/commentaire-ose-immuno-03-03-2026. Nothing independent confirms the slip itself.

outside_window.finding: ARTEMIA Phase 3 interim futility outcome at the October 2026 IDMC review. A binary of the whole thesis with sign unknown, easily +/-20-40% when it lands.
Combi-TED Phase 2 topline (Tedopi plus nivolumab or docetaxel, 2L NSCLC), ESMO rapid oral on 25 Oct 2026, abstract 2661 RO. The data were not disclosed in the 23 Sep release.

baseline_tension: The findings run with the tape's down-trend (run-up -27.65% over 20 days, -12.24% over 5, -38.19% over 60) and against the +1.38 bounce lean. With no short-register anchor to beat, the negative is probably mostly in the price already, so the emitted -0.8 sits 0.5 below the -1.3 finding sum.
language_note: French independent biotech commentary (Biomed Impact) framed the market's expectation that the IRIS line is a bridge to a larger raise within 3-6 months, and flagged refinancing as 'central sur le dossier' on 3 Sep. The English wire copy carries only the company's framing ('first step of a global financing strategy').

The French AMF voting-rights filings ('Informations relatives au nombre total de droits de vote', French only, never issued in English) are the only place the monthly IRIS draw-downs (200k/466k/599k shares) are disclosed. That is the input to the proceeds shortfall in finding 1.
French retail forums (Boursorama) show the Q3 ARTEMIA futility timing being actively watched and IRIS selling blamed for the slide. This is context only, not used as evidence.
The French investor page and the AMF-filed calendar confirm the 28 Sep date identically to the English page; the after-close statement appears on the English page.
lessons_applied: 'Financing is a question, not a verdict': the financing finding went from -1.5 to -1.0, and its band widened to +8 on the upside, because a sizeable raise that ends the IRIS overhang can read as relief. Biomed Impact says so explicitly.

'The hunter's own caveat has to reach the number' and 'positioning is the thing to beat': the negative agrees with a 50% slide and adds nothing to a register that is only a truncated zero, so the expected move went from -1.5 to -0.8, visibly below the -1.3 sum.

'Keep findings inside the exit window': the ARTEMIA futility outcome (October IDMC) and the Combi-TED ESMO data (25 Oct) stay in outside_window. Only the re-dating residual stays in findings, trimmed from -0.5 to -0.3 because the February release already telegraphed October.
'Coverage tells you which regime you are in' (band 3-7): noted, but I did not size up. These facts are the discussed ones on this name, not a confirmed fact nobody is positioned for.
